_doc: EMBERBROOK — THE CINEMATIC CAMERAS. Hand-authored companion to emberbrook.map.json:
the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF7/8/9 grammar).
Schema is dellhollow.cameras.json's, exactly — read that file's _doc for the full
contract (ownership, framing intent, arrival overrides, exits-in-frame). What is
written HERE is only what is different about this town.
THE SHOT LIST IS ELEVEN, and docs/plans/emberbrook-town.md §4's table is six of them.
THE SIX (arch, square, pondlane, homerow, northlane, gatefield) are that table transcribed,
written for a town half this size. THE OTHER FIVE were authorised by the coordinator on
2026-08-01 after the 2x round measured what the six could actually deliver — five of them
could not reach cine_test's 50 px legibility floor at ANY of 468 swept angles, because a
35-degree lens holds about 20 m of span at 50 px and the redline doubled every distance in
the map. Dellhollow plays through sixteen shots over 100 m; six over 180 m was never going
to hold. In order along the player's own walk:
woodroad   the arrival clearing, the game's first frame       63 px
waystone   the stone, where the sketchbook and the world agree 76 px
arch       the village arch                                    51 px
orchard    the rows and the cider press                        50 px
therise    the climb, where the village comes over the crest   73 px
square     Festival Square                                     39 px  <- the one under-floor shot
pondlane   the pond, the jetty, the footbridge                 50 px
homerow    Lake's round, first leg                             58 px
northlane  the walled climb to the tithe barn                  58 px
gateroad   the quiet road, mid-seclusion                       57 px
gatefield  the Old Gate court                                  54 px
TEN OF ELEVEN CLEAR THE FLOOR. The eleventh is Festival Square and it is not a camera
problem: the 2x builder emits the plaza as ONE 27.9 x 27.9 m walk mesh, ownership is per
mesh, and the coordinator's own FFIX approach-shot proposal was built (`therise`) and
measured — it lifted the square 33 -> 39 px and lifted THE ARCH 44 -> 51. The across-the-
square half of that pattern needs the builder to emit the plaza as cells. See square's
`_charPxMin_why`, which is now the only charPxMin ratchet left in the file.
Every landmark and every one of the map's 23 walk edges has exactly one owner, every shot
owns >=10 m of route and the junction it hangs off, and no map edge changes the camera more
than once — except `barn__gate-court` and `road-gate__square-plaza`, which change it twice
each because `gateroad` and `therise` are declared `thresholdPair`, the only mechanism
seam-canon 2 allows and the only two shots in the town that are places you enter and leave.
A SHOT THAT WAS PROPOSED, BUILT AND WITHDRAWN, recorded because the refusal is the finding:
`washgreen`, a twelfth camera for the washline green. It measured 90-116 px and it is not
here, because the green is a 12.7 m dead-end spur and the two windows do not intersect —
no-sliver (seam-canon 3) needs the shot to own >=10 m of that edge, i.e. a boundary at
t<=0.21, and no-path-overlap (seam-canon 5) needs t>=0.35 or the seam band lies across the
weir's pad and the footbridge lane. Pond Lane re-absorbed the green and still clears the
floor at 50 px, so the town is better with eleven shots than with twelve.
THE MID-EDGE SPLITS WERE ALL RE-DERIVED AT 2x ON 2026-08-01, and this is the single
most consequential change in that round after the cameras themselves. A split exists
to put the seam where the plaza NARROWS TO A LANE (§4's articulation), and the four
authored fractions were measured against the 1x plaza: pond 0.352, home 0.569, north
0.573, bridge 0.445. On the 2x floor those fractions land INSIDE the plaza, and the
band's half-width is measured off the walk surface — so a seam standing on a 25 m
plaza measured 12.4 u wide against the 13 u cap, and seam_test found a player walking
from the Heartlight to the ITEM SHOP crossing two camera cuts on the way. Re-measured
on the current bundle by walking each edge and asking which mesh the ground belongs
to, the plaza's own floor ends at t=0.633 (pond lane, 14.4 m out), t=0.717 (home lane,
17.1 m) and t=0.567 (north lane, 13.8 m) — all roughly DOUBLE the 1x distances the old
fractions were set from, which is exactly what a 2x scale does to a distance. The
splits are now 0.78 / 0.73 / 0.573, and the bands they produce are 1.4 to 2.95 u wide.
THE BRIDGE DIAGONAL LOST ITS SPLIT ENTIRELY: at extent 14 the plaza's floor now covers
the WHOLE of `brook-bridge__square-plaza` (the footbridge at (76,52) is 14.4 m from
the plaza centre, i.e. on its rim), so no fraction on that edge is outside the plaza.
`square` takes all of it and the cut falls back to the endpoint rule — 2.8 m from the
footbridge, on the bridge's own narrow approach, band 2.25 u. Pond Lane still owns the
bridge itself and still needs no thresholdPair.
AND THE QUIET ROAD GAINED ONE: `barn__gate-court` is split at t=0.80 rather than left
to the endpoint rule, which put the seam 2.8 m from the gate court's centre — INSIDE
an area of extent 10, band 10.3 u wide, and seam_test caught the consequence exactly
where it hurts: walking the court to the Whisperwood stile fired the gate cut twice
and a positional correction. At 0.80 the seam is 11.7 m out on the road where the band
is 2.25 u, `gatefield` owns the last 11.7 m of its own approach, and the court is one
unbroken piece of ground again.
THRESHOLD PAIRS: NONE, and that is a ruling, not an omission. Emberbrook has no
bridge or stairwell that is a place you ENTER AND LEAVE — the brook footbridge lives
INSIDE pondlane (it owns both of the bridge's edges and the bridge itself), so its
passage costs one cut like any other. `thresholdPair` is declared the day a shot owns
the middle of an edge whose two ends belong to other cameras, and on nothing else (§2).
frameExits: true FROM THE FIRST COMMIT. Dellhollow opts out because its backdrops
predate the flag; Emberbrook has no such debt and never will.
THE GRADE IS THE EMBERWAKE EVENING and it lives in TWO fields of `defaults`, which
together are its single source: `exposure` (the view transform) and `lightRig` (the
sun, the sky, and the census of the lamps the town's light actually comes out of).
tools/cine_bake.py reads both through the solved file, so the blend cannot drift from
the deliverable. See defaults._grade_why.

defaults._frameExits_why: Town-wide from the first commit (emberbrook-town.md §4). Every shot frames the seams it exits by, so a player can neither appear nor walk off-screen.
defaults._doc_minDist: Floor on the solved standoff. Dellhollow's is 15 against a canyon town whose tiers stack 5 m apart; Emberbrook is a village whose plaza is 14 m across and whose buildings are 5-8 m tall, so 15 would stand every shot outside its own district. 12 still keeps a camera out of the geometry it is framing, and four of five districts are still gray blockout — a shot solved against massing must leave room for the art that replaces it.
defaults._doc_maxDist: THE LEASH, RE-RULED 2026-08-01 FOR THE 2x TOWN (was 46, a 1x number, and the only reason five of the seven shots solved `capped`). maxDist binds ONLY when a region does not fit inside it, and a capped shot is a CROPPED shot: the solver stops backing off and part of the ground the shot owns falls outside its own frame, which is the one thing exit-framing exists to prevent. Set to 66 because that is the longest standoff any of the seven solved shots actually asks for (northlane's 56.4 m over its 47 m of road) plus headroom; every other shot solves between 27 and 48 m and is untouched by the change, because a cap is not a target. It is NOT doubled to 92 with the rest of the map: a leash that no shot can reach stops being a leash, and the number's whole job is to make an over-long region fail loudly instead of quietly standing the camera in the next district.
_grade_why: THE EMBERWAKE EVENING. Chapter One IS this hour, and the two shipped, accepted
Chapter One paintings are already lit by it: public/assets/scenes/square/festival.png
is the Heartlight's amber flame centre-frame with the plaza in lamplight and a dark
blue sky, and entrance/main.png is the waystone at dusk with the village warm through
the arch. So this is not a departure from the project's ratified golden hour — it is
the key the town's own accepted art direction was painted in, and golden hour is one
re-run away (the A/B is on the morning board, docs/qa/emberbrook/index.html).
The grade is TWO numbers and no more: `exposure` here, and `lightRig` below. Neither
is written anywhere else — cine_bake.py applies both, so the master blend and the
shipped plate cannot disagree about what hour it is.

_doc: THE TOWN'S LIGHT, as data. Applied by tools/cine_bake.py at bake time to the objects
named here; a town with no lightRig (Dellhollow) is untouched and bakes byte-identical.
It lives in the CAMERA file rather than in the builder because the grade is a camera-lane
ruling and the builder's blend is another lane's file: this way the bake can be re-run in
either key without a rebuild, and the key that shipped is recorded beside the plates.

sun._why: The last of it, raking. The blockout's own golden key is energy 3.6 at (56,0,212); this is the same sun an hour later and 20 degrees round.

_why: The sky has gone blue and stopped being the light source: the blockout's golden key
is 1.15. RULED AT 0.55 on 2026-07-31, and the number is the only one in this file that
was chosen by sweeping three different knobs and finding that two of them do nothing.
THE MEASUREMENT. Median luminance of the pixels each shot's own region probes land on
— the GROUND THE PLAYER WALKS, not the frame, because a frame can be bright and its
floor unreadable — as a fraction of the same shot in the ratified golden hour:
TRIPLING THE ORDINARY LAMPS CHANGES THE WALKED GROUND BY TWO PER CENT, and the pool
contrast (p90:p10 of the ground samples) does not move either — 2.5:1 stays 2.6:1 at
the arch, 7.7:1 stays 7.7:1 on Home Row. If the lamps were making pools, more watts
would raise the bright tail; they do not. The lamps light their posts and the few
metres under them, and none of the floor a camera frames. THE SUN DOES NOTHING EITHER,
and that follows from its own angle: at 80 degrees it rakes almost horizontally, so it
lights vertical faces and skips the ground. A `lampW` knob was authorised and then NOT
built, because shipping a knob whose own test says it does nothing is worse than
shipping no knob.
SO THE SKY IS THE WHOLE LEVER, and 0.55 is where it is set because contrast is the
identity. It buys the arch — the game's first frame — a fifth of its ground back
(0.32x -> 0.38x), leaves the Old Gate emphatically dark now that its lamp has been
withdrawn (0.25x), and does not touch the two shots the lamps genuinely carry. It
keeps the pool-to-pool walk that IS Chapter One: Home Row 7.7:1 -> 5.8:1, Pond Lane
5.4:1 -> 4.5:1. sky 0.80 would put the arch at 0.44x and the gate at 0.33x, inside the
0.4-0.55 target, and costs the arch's contrast 2.5:1 -> 1.8:1 and Home Row's -> 4.7:1;
it is the named alternative on the morning board and it is one field and one re-bake.
The 0.38x miss against the 0.40 floor is accepted knowingly: the sky becoming a light
source again is the one thing this key exists to stop.
ASSERTED AT BAKE TIME, because this grade only works if the light is where the story
says it is. Emberbrook is the rare survivor that still HAS a Heartlight: exactly one
source over 2000 W (the pedestal, 5200 W) and fourteen ordinary 680 W lampposts lit
FROM it. KEYEMB_lamp_00..14 are the LIGHTS (the `KEY*` prefix is this project's
light-naming canon; the posts themselves are the `emb_lamp_*` meshes) and they are
numbered in LAKE'S CANONICAL ROUNDS ORDER (STORY.md §2,
the map's own lamps{} block): low ground first — Pond Lane, where the moths rise off
the water — then inward, CLOSING THE RING at the lamps nearest the Heartlight. Lighting
COUNT RULING 2026-07-31: FOURTEEN, not fifteen. The gate-court lamp was withdrawn —
chapter1.js and the plan agree that the Old Gate is the one place in the village
nobody's warmth reaches, and the shipped gate/gray.png is nearly monochrome for that
reason. The roll renumbered behind it; the bake prints it, so the count in this file
and the lamps in the blend cannot drift apart without failing.
them by name stages the canon for free; the bake prints the roll in that order so the
staging is checkable and not just believed.
The Heartlight's SURFACE emission stays at 26 and is not touched here: at 180 the
crystal rendered as a clipped white hole with no crystal in it. The brightness belongs
to the 5200 W lamp beside it; the surface only has to glow.

cameras.name: The Whisperwood Road
cameras.shot: THE GAME'S FIRST FRAME. The quiet road through the Whisperwood at dusk, looking north the way Vesper is walking: the arrival clearing behind her, the wood pressing close on both sides and closing the sky, the mossy waystone standing on the verge with EMBERBROOK cut into it, and the road climbing gently away past it toward a warmth that is not yet a village — no roof, no arch, no lamp in frame, only the light on the road. The village is a rumour until the next shot.
cameras._framing_note: DUE SOUTH ON THE ROAD'S OWN AXIS, which is the shot's own sentence — the camera stands behind her and she walks away up the road into frame. 63 px at a 27.3 m standoff, 90.0% of 40 chest-and-head probes visible. THE PITCH MOVED 18 -> 26 WHEN THE SHOT LOST THE WAYSTONE: at 37 m of road under one camera the low angle was the only one that held any character height at all (42 px at pitch 18) and it was bought against the wood, which closes below 18 degrees — p10 measures 0% visible, i.e. the camera inside the trunks. Split at the clearing's own end the region is 9.9 x 14.6 m, the standoff halves, and pitch 26 costs nothing: 63 px, and the trees are above the lens instead of across it. The column at yaw 270 reads p18 58 px / 88%, p26 63 / 90%, p30 62 / 90%.
cameras._owns_note: MINTED 2026-08-01 (camera lane, this handover). p-woodroad was minted at the 2x round as 'the game's opening scene' and then had no shot: chapter1.js beats 1-3 (the intro narration, the sketchbook recognition at the stone, Mochi hiring himself) all stage here, and the overworld's `emberbrook-gate` portal lands on this ground — measured at runtime (52.8, -0.5, 24.8) — so before this camera existed the FIRST THING THE GAME DID was materialise the player in a scene no camera owned. cine_test said so in as many words: "Enter Emberbrook: arrives in a solved shot (cam null)". `entry: true` moves here from `arch` for the same reason: the cut graph's root is the shot the town is entered by.
cameras._splits_why: THE ONE SPLIT IS `waystone__road-gate` AT t=0.45, and it is the same instrument as the arch's own split at the other end of the same road. The two edges of the wood road are 16.5 m (clearing->waystone) and 20.4 m (waystone->arch); giving the whole second edge to `arch` would put the cut ON the waystone, which is the one piece of ground in this parcel a scripted beat stands still on — the player would walk up to the stone and change camera at the moment they reached it. Split at 0.45 this shot keeps the stone and 9.2 m of road past it (25.7 m owned in total) and `arch` gets 11.2 m, both clear of seam-canon 3's 10 m no-sliver floor. The cut lands where the map's own edge note says the scene changes anyway: "the last stretch: the wood thins, the arch and the first lamplight appear".

cameras.name: The Waystone
cameras.shot: The stone on the verge, and the second frame the game shows. Closer and lower than the clearing: the mossy marker standing off the road's west side with EMBERBROOK cut into it under the lichen and the hand-scratched note beneath that, the road going on past it up the last rise, and the wood still shoulder to shoulder on both sides. This is where Vesper's sketchbook and the waking world agree for the first time, and where Mochi hires himself.
cameras._framing_note: CLOSE AND SLIGHTLY OFF-AXIS, and the brightest legibility in the town after the Rise: 76 px at 22.2 m, 98.4% of 64 probes. yaw 280 rather than 270 because the stone stands on the road's WEST verge and a camera dead on the axis puts it against the centre of frame with the road behind it; ten degrees round sets it screen-left with the road running past it, which is the composition the shot's text describes and the one that lets a player read the stone as a thing beside the way rather than a thing in it. The pitch column at yaw 280 is flat from 26 to 38 (76, 76, 74 px at 98%), so 30 is chosen on composition rather than on the number — high enough to show the road's surface, low enough that the wood still closes the top of frame.
cameras._owns_note: MINTED 2026-08-01, the fourth and last of the shots the coordinator authorised, and the one that finally lets the opening walk be FF grammar rather than one long held frame. p-woodroad is 37 m of road carrying three scripted beats — the intro narration on the clearing, the sketchbook recognition at the stone, Mochi hiring himself — and one camera over all of it read 42 px. Split, the clearing reads 63 px and the stone 76, both at the road's own bearing and both above 90% visible. THE CUT IS AT t=0.65 OF `arrival-clearing__waystone`, WHICH IS 5.8 m SHORT OF THE STONE, and that number is the whole reason the split is on this edge rather than at the junction: a boundary at the waystone node itself would put the camera change ON the one piece of ground in this parcel that a scripted beat stands still on, and the player would reach the stone and change shot in the same step. One cut on each of the two edges, both internal, neither on a landmark.

cameras.name: The Village Arch
cameras.shot: Arrival, and the game's first frame. From inside the village on the high west shoulder, looking back south down the road: the orchard rows falling away on the right with their ladders and baskets, the waystone on the bend, the timber arch and its harvest wreaths at the bottom of the road, and the valley the player has walked up beyond it. The road runs AWAY from camera, so the arch reads as a threshold you came through rather than a door you are about to open.
cameras._framing_note: THE PLAN'S OWN BEARING, RESTORED, AND NOW OVER THE FLOOR. yaw 260 is the ratified third measurement from the 1x round — 'stands the camera SOUTH of the arch looking north, the composition public/assets/scenes/entrance/main.png already accepted' — and this round it finally measures well enough to keep: 51 px at 30.4 m, 71.9% of 64 probes. The 2x re-solve had been forced 20 degrees off it (280/26, 31 px) because the arch was then a THREE-ARMED JUNCTION carrying the wood road, the orchard spur and the whole 37.6 m climb; `orchard` and `therise` took two of those arms this round and the region fell from 31 x 38 m to 14.9 x 28 m. PITCH 10 IS THE PRICE AND IT IS PAID DELIBERATELY: the column at yaw 260 reads p10 51 px / 72%, p18 44 / 69%, p26 39 / 77%, p34 36 / 86% — visibility rises with pitch and legibility falls, and 72% against the blockout's own cone-trees is the softest number in the shipped set. It is also, for this shot alone, the RIGHT compositional end of that trade: a low camera makes a 4 m timber arch loom over the road, and a high one makes it a hoop on the ground. FLAGGED FOR THE BOARD with the render, as its predecessor was.
cameras._owns_note: river-vista is p-entrance dressing (the valley river Vesper has followed for weeks, glimpsed east of the road on arrival). It is not walkable and carries no pad, so it costs this shot nothing but the totality assertion it satisfies. | CORRECTED 2026-08-01: this shot claimed two edges THAT HAVE NEVER EXISTED IN THIS MAP — `road-gate__waystone` and `waystone__orchard`. The map's edges are `waystone__road-gate` (the other way round, and since the 2x round it starts outside the village) and `road-gate__orchard` (the orchard spur branches from INSIDE the arch — retyped by the same stamp that moved the waystone out). cine_solve had been printing both as warnings since the 2x round while the totality assertion passed on the strings, which is exactly the failure the seclusion stamp's own note warns about: coverage is proved by matching these strings against the map's own records, so a string that matches nothing proves nothing. The waystone itself moves to the `woodroad` shot with the parcel it left in; this shot keeps the last 11.2 m of that road (t 0.45..1) and picks up the orchard spur and the cider press, which is the p-entrance parcel exactly.

cameras.name: The Orchard Rows
cameras.shot: The harvest, and the only frame in the town that is WORK rather than home. Broadside across the rows from the road's own side: apple trees in ranks stepping away west with their ladders still against them and baskets under them, the open-sided cider press closing the frame with its crates and straw and the smell of the pressing, and the arch's lamp small back down the spur behind. Emberwake is the payoff of autumn and this is the ground it was grown on.
cameras._framing_note: BROADSIDE FROM THE ROAD SIDE, LOOKING WEST ALONG THE ROWS. yaw 90 puts the camera east of the block so the ranks recede across frame instead of pointing at the lens, which is the only way rows read as rows; 50 px at 33.2 m, 90.0% of 10 probes. The pitch column at yaw 90 is the whole decision and it is a straight trade: p30 52 px / 60% visible, p34 52 / 80%, p38 50 / 90%, p42 49 / 100%. 38 is the first angle that clears both the town's 50 px floor and a 90% sightline; 42 would buy the last ten points of visibility with the floor itself. The occluder below 34 degrees is the orchard's own canopy — the correct kind, and the reason this shot is not lower.
cameras._owns_note: MINTED 2026-08-01 on the coordinator's shot-grammar ruling, and it is a SPLIT OF `arch` rather than a new place: `walk_lm_orchard` is a single 19.8 x 19.8 m mesh and `road-gate` stands 26 m from its centre, so one camera holding both was holding a 31 x 38 m region and reading 31 px against a 50 px floor. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS MEASURED FIRST AND REFUSED: trimming the arch's two road arms instead (0.62 of the wood road to `woodroad`, 0.28 of the climb to `square`) moves it from 35 px to 38 px and clears the floor at ZERO of 468 angles — the orchard lobe is the whole of the problem and no amount of arm-trimming touches it. Split, the arch reads a 56 px ceiling and the rows 55 px.

cameras.name: The Rise
cameras.shot: THE REVEAL, and the only shot in the town whose subject is a thing that happens rather than a thing that stands. The climb from the arch up to the square, taken from off the road's west shoulder: the cobbles running up and away, the orchard's last rows falling behind on the left, and over the crest of the rise the village arriving one roof at a time — chimney smoke, then thatch, then the bunting, and the Heartlight's glow on the undersides of it all before the flame itself is in sight. Chapter One's beat 4 is walked here.
cameras._framing_note: LOW, CLOSE, AND LOOKING STRAIGHT UP THE CLIMB — 73 px at 20.1 m with 100.0% of 50 probes visible, the cleanest sightline in the town. yaw 270 stands the camera below the rise on the road's own axis so the cobbles run away from the lens and the village comes over the crest ahead of the player rather than beside them; pitch 10 is the lowest angle in the whole shipped set and it is the point of the shot, because a reveal over a crest only exists if the crest is between the camera and the thing revealed. The column at yaw 270 reads p10 73 px / 100%, p14 69 / 100%, p18 65 / 84%, p26 59 / 48% — the visibility collapse above 18 degrees is the rise itself entering the sightline from a camera high enough to look over it, which is the same fact stated backwards.
cameras._owns_note: MINTED 2026-08-01, and it is the coordinator's own (b) answered somewhere other than where the question pointed. The brief asked whether the FFIX plaza pattern — an approach shot plus an across-the-square shot — could lift Festival Square off its 33 px floor. THE ACROSS-THE-SQUARE HALF IS NOT AVAILABLE AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, not a taste call: the 2x builder emits the plaza as ONE 27.9 x 27.9 m walk mesh (`walk_lm_square-plaza`), ownership is per mesh, so a second camera inside the square could own nothing but the door spurs and the road stubs — 5.8 m of route and every mesh inside its neighbour's pad, which is `quay-east` verbatim, the shot that produced a user complaint within an hour of live play. THE APPROACH HALF IS available, because the ROAD ships its own ribbon meshes: this shot. It does not help the square (measured at 38 px with the approach split off it, against 37 without — the plaza is the constraint and the road arm never was), and it lifts THE ARCH from 44 px to 59. The arch was a three-armed junction — the wood road south, the orchard spur west, the climb north — and this takes the longest arm off it. 15.8 m of route, two cuts on `road-gate__square-plaza` and both of them this shot's own abutments, which is what `thresholdPair` means. It supersedes the 2026-07-31 ruling that split this edge once at t=0.45 to close the p-entrance/p-square gutter: the gutter is still closed, by a shot instead of by a boundary.

cameras.name: Festival Square
cameras.shot: The postcard of home. Across the plaza from the north, with the Heartlight on its pedestal centre-frame and brightest — the inn's stone steps and lit windows to the right, the item shop and the notice board to the left, the bakery's warm window closing the west side, stalls and bunting around the ring, and the road running away south down the rise the player just climbed. This is the frame Chapter One takes away.
cameras._charPxMin_why: 38 px, and THE LAST UNDER-FLOOR SHOT IN THE TOWN — the other ten clear 50 px after the shot-grammar round. It is set at 38 against a measured 39, and it is the ONLY ratchet left because it is the only one no camera work can lift. THREE INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS SAY THE SAME THING. (1) An ownership variant handing the four lane-head stubs to their neighbours and leaving this camera the bare plaza scores 35 px, WORSE than the 37 it had with them. (2) `therise` took the ENTIRE 15.8 m approach arm off this shot this round, which is the coordinator's own FFIX approach-shot proposal built and measured: the region fell from 32.5 x 35.6 m to 32.5 x 28.7 m and the shot moved 33 -> 39 px, still eleven short. (3) The across-the-square half of that proposal CANNOT BE BUILT from this lane at all: the 2x builder emits the plaza as ONE 27.9 x 27.9 m walk mesh (`walk_lm_square-plaza`), ownership is per mesh, so a second camera inside the square could own nothing but door spurs and road stubs — 5.8 m of route with every mesh inside its neighbour's pad, which is `quay-east` verbatim and the shot that drew a user complaint inside an hour of live play. THE UNBLOCKING CHANGE IS THE BUILDER'S, NOT THIS FILE'S: emit the plaza floor as CELLS the way the 1x blockout did (its own arrival notes describe 'a cell grid with the pedestal's footprint cut out'), and a north/south pair of shots on a ~14 m half each lands where the gate court's 17.9 m region already sits, which is 54 px. Until then this shot carries the 2x scale's bill for the town's hero frame, knowingly, at 39 px.
cameras._arrivals_why_2x: ONE OVERRIDE SURVIVES THE 2x RE-SEARCH, and it is a different point for a different reason than the four that were withdrawn. Coming back down the north lane into the square, the DERIVED arrival lands at (64.55, -55.02) and the walk network has a HOLE there: probed on a 1 m lattice, the plaza's cell floor reads 1.500 at x 62-63 and x 66-67 all the way to y=57, and reads NOTHING at x 64.0-65.0, y=55 — the lane ribbon's own footprint, cut out of the plaza floor one metre south of where the ribbon itself starts (its first surface is 1.902 at y=56). So the arrival is in a slot on the road's centreline, 1 m long. Searched by the method in `_arrivals_why` — 0.15 m lattice over this shot's own ground, on the walk network, on THIS camera's ground, same side of the band, ranked by solid footing then smallest teleport — over 3137 admissible points: (64.141, 1.500, -54.459) is 0.78 m from the derived point, has ground under all nine samples of a 0.6 m body box, and clears the band by 2.26 m against a 1.6 m target. It is the only one of the five 1x overrides whose PROBLEM survived the rescale, and unlike them it now beats the target instead of trading against it. The hole itself is a blockout artifact and belongs to the builder's lane, not this one: an area floor should not cut a slot for a ribbon that starts a metre further on. Filed, not fixed here.
_arrivals_withdrawn: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-01 (camera lane, 2x round), and withdrawn rather than rescaled. Four
overrides stood here — pondlane x2, homerow, northlane — every one of them a point SEARCHED
those four points land 25 m south-west of it, in the orchard. Doubling them is not the fix
either: an override is a point that was proved to be on the walk network, on this camera's
own ground, outside the band and clear of it — four properties of a floor that has been
rebuilt twice since, so the arithmetic would carry the coordinates over and leave every one
of the proofs behind. The derived arrivals are re-measured at 2x below; the search is
re-runnable and the reasoning that produced these four is preserved verbatim in
`_arrivals_why` because it is the METHOD, and the method did not go stale.
RE-MEASURED: the 2x plaza no longer has the holes that forced them. All four derived
arrivals land on the walk network and inside their receiving shot's frame with no override
at all — the cell floor the 1x builder cut around the pedestal and the buildings is now a
25 x 27 m plaza with 6-13 m of clear ground between the lip and each building, so the first
point past each band is real ground. cine_test's GRAPH section is the check and it is green.
cameras._arrivals_why: AUTHORED BECAUSE THE PLAZA HAD HOLES IN IT AT 1x — kept as the METHOD, not as live data (see _arrivals_withdrawn), not because the seams are wrong. Festival Square's floor is a cell grid with the Heartlight pedestal's and the buildings' footprints cut out of it, measured at 0.1 m over the whole plaza: about 42 m2 of clear cells in a 12.7 x 13.5 m box, with the centre (30-33, 21-23) almost entirely cut away and the rows at y=26 and y=29-30 empty where the brook crosses. A derived arrival is the first point along the path clear of the band, and five of them land in those gaps — reported by cutGeometry as 'is off the walk network'. Each override below was SEARCHED, not typed: a 0.15 m grid over the receiving shot's own ground, keeping only points that are on the walk network, on THIS camera's ground, outside the band on the same side as the derived point, and clear of it by more than the 0.5 m floor; ranked by solid footing first (a 0.6 m body box with ground under all nine samples), then by the SMALLEST teleport, because the player feels the jump. cutGeometry re-checks every one of them and rejects it loudly otherwise. The two east ones clear the band by 0.58 m and 0.50 m against a 1.6 m target: that is the co-located-twin frontier's own cost — both bands sit within 1.2 m of each other by design (seam-canon 5.1), so there is nowhere further to stand that is still on the plaza. Above the floor, so accepted with the documented warning: clearance traded for an arrival on real ground rather than in a hole.
_splits_why: THE FOUR LANE HEADS ARE AUTHORED SPLITS AT THE PLAZA'S LIP, and they are the
difference between a junction and a strobe. `square-plaza` is an AREA of extent 7 and
`cutOffset` is 2.8, so every DERIVED seam leaving this shot would sit 2.8 m from the
landmark's position — which is the Heartlight's own pedestal. Four camera cuts in a
5.6 m circle around the town's hero prop is the quay junction verbatim (seam-canon §3),
and it is worse than that: the plaza floor is a cell grid with the pedestal's footprint
CUT OUT of its centre, so each seam's backward arrival lands in the hole. Measured
before the fix: `arrival (32.1, 22.0) is off the walk network`, three times.
So the seams are authored where the plaza NARROWS TO A LANE — the articulation
seam-canon §4 asks for. The distances are measured, not chosen: the plaza's cell floor
is the last surface under the pond lane at 6.5 m, under the home lane at 6.0 m, under
the north lane at 6.0 m, and under the bridge diagonal at 5.2 m from the plaza centre.
Each split is set just past its own lip. This is also, exactly, what 'the square owns
the head of every departing road' has to mean when the road starts at an area's centre.
cameras._owns_note: ONE PLAZA, ONE CAMERA, and it owns the HEADS OF ALL SIX departing roads as well as the floor, so no seam has to sit inside the junction (seam-canon §8; the loop stairs taught this by needing two seams inside seven metres). A tighter shot on the same floor would be a zoom, not a cut — `quay-east` owned 5.8 m of route inside its neighbour's own pad and produced a user complaint inside an hour of live play (§3).
cameras._framing_note: FROM THE NORTH AND HIGHER STILL: yaw 90 HELD on its own ruling, pitch 46 -> 50. The north bearing survives every re-solve for the reason it was chosen — the plaza's solid neighbours (inn, item shop, notice board, bakery) are all south or west of it and only the well's low ring stands north — and the sweep agrees: at yaw 90 the visibility column reads p42 81%, p46 86%, p50 93.8%, p58 93.8%, flattening at 50, while charPxFar sits at 39-40 across the whole column. So the pitch is chosen on sightline alone, because legibility does not move: this shot is against its own floor at every angle and the reason is in `_charPxMin_why`, not here. The standoff fell 47.6 -> 41.9 m when `therise` took the approach arm.

cameras.name: Pond Lane
cameras.shot: The quiet one. Low along the shore looking back west up the lane, the pond filling the near half of frame with the Heartlight's glow lying on the water, the jetty's piles in silhouette, the plank footbridge over the brook mid-frame and the washing lines on the green to the right. Frogs, fireflies, and the last lamp of Lake's round out at the jetty.
cameras._framing_note: WEST OF THE WATER, LOOKING BACK EAST ACROSS IT — AND THAT IS A REVERSAL OF A RATIFIED RULING, ON A MEASUREMENT. 50 px at 25.4 m, 89.1% of 64 probes, with all nine of the pond's own rim points, the jetty and the footbridge in frame. THE RULING IT OVERTURNS: the 1x note put this camera east of the pond and paid 14 px for it, because 'the Heartlight's glow mirrored in the pond' (the map's own p-lane intent) 'is only visible from the far side of the water from its source'. That is true of a MIRROR IMAGE and this pond cannot carry one. Measured over all 468 swept camera positions: the specular bounce point — where the flame's reflection would land, at hz/(hz+cz) of the way from flame to camera — comes no closer than 14.8 m to the pond centre against a 9 m radius, and lands on the water for ZERO of them. The arithmetic is not close: the flame sits 2.7 m above the water and 29.1 m away, and every camera in the sweep stands 15-45 m up, so the image never leaves the flame's own few metres of the plaza. WHAT THE POND CAN CARRY IS A DIFFUSE GLOW, and a diffuse glow has no preferred side — so the constraint that forced the east family is withdrawn and the choice of bank becomes a lighting question for the dressing lane and the user at bake time, not a camera one. FLAGGED FOR THE BOARD. Inside the released family, yaw 220 pitch 30 is the best frame that holds the whole pond: the east family's own ceiling WITH the pond in frame is 44 px, six short of the floor and eleven short of this.
cameras._arrivals_withdrawn: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-01 with the square's three (see that camera's `_arrivals_withdrawn`): (38.00, 1.33, -25.50) was searched on the 1x footbridge pad and the 2x footbridge is at map (76, 52). Re-derived clean.
cameras._arrivals_why: AUTHORED BECAUSE THE PLAZA HAD HOLES IN IT AT 1x — kept as the METHOD, not as live data. Festival Square's floor is a cell grid with the Heartlight pedestal's and the buildings' footprints cut out of it, measured at 0.1 m over the whole plaza: about 42 m2 of clear cells in a 12.7 x 13.5 m box, with the centre (30-33, 21-23) almost entirely cut away and the rows at y=26 and y=29-30 empty where the brook crosses. A derived arrival is the first point along the path clear of the band, and five of them land in those gaps — reported by cutGeometry as 'is off the walk network'. Each override below was SEARCHED, not typed: a 0.15 m grid over the receiving shot's own ground, keeping only points that are on the walk network, on THIS camera's ground, outside the band on the same side as the derived point, and clear of it by more than the 0.5 m floor; ranked by solid footing first (a 0.6 m body box with ground under all nine samples), then by the SMALLEST teleport, because the player feels the jump. cutGeometry re-checks every one of them and rejects it loudly otherwise. This one is cheap: 0.71 m onto the footbridge's own pad, clearing 2.18 m.
_seam_findings_2x: TWO seam_test FAILURES ARE LEFT STANDING WITH THEIR MEASUREMENTS, because both are facts
about the ground rather than about a camera, and papering over either would move a seam
somewhere worse.
1. `walk_pad_pips-den` OVERLAPS THE POND LANE. Every seam position in the slide window of
the square<->pondlane cut crosses it, at EVERY split fraction from t=0.63 (where the plaza
floor ends) to t=0.97 (where the jetty pad begins) — measured by sweeping t and reading the
warning. The pad's box is rt x 77.2..80.1, z -49.2..-46.7 and the lane's ribbon runs
z -47.9..-45.4 through the same x, so they share ground: there is no seam on this lane that
does not cross Pip's den. t=0.78 is chosen because it is the LEAST harmful of the
unavoidable overlaps — the den is pondlane's OWN landmark, so a player walking to it is
walking into pondlane and being cut there is correct, whereas every t past 0.80 overlaps
`pond-jetty__brook-bridge` instead, which is pondlane at BOTH ends: a cut there would flip
the camera on a player who never left the shot. FOR THE BUILDER'S LANE: the den's own stamp
says it sits 'under the bank, hidden from the lane', and its walk pad is on the lane.
2. TOWN-WIDE MISMATCH 4.3 m AGAINST A 4.1 m BUDGET, i.e. 0.2 m over, on the town's ONE
remaining endpoint seam. The budget is cutOffset x endpoint-seams x 1.45 and the split
re-derivation took the count from four to one, so the budget shrank faster than the
mismatch did. The 4.3 m is `brook-bridge__square-plaza`, where the plaza's own floor now
covers the whole edge: the cut sits 2.8 m from the footbridge and the floor changes hands
at the bridge's pad, and those two points cannot be made to coincide while the plaza owns
the ground under the seam. AN INTERNAL SPLIT AT t=0.19 WAS TRIED AND MEASURED WORSE, not
argued away: seam_test went from 2 failures to 15, because a seam that close to the bridge
puts the band on the `pond-jetty__brook-bridge` ribbon and the walk oscillates.
Reverted, and the 0.2 m is accepted with this note.
cameras._owns_note: THE BROOK FOOTBRIDGE LIVES INSIDE THIS SHOT — it owns the bridge landmark AND both of the bridge's edges, so walking the lane out and the bridge back is one cut each way and this camera needs no `thresholdPair`. A bridge only costs two cuts when a shot owns the MIDDLE of an edge whose two ends belong to other cameras (dellhollow's Crossing); that is not the shape here. brook-mouth is the town's name made visible (the confluence east of the pond) and has a pad but no edge — it is p-lane's by bounds and this shot frames it.

cameras.name: Home Row
cameras.shot: Lake's round, first leg. Broadside to the home lane from below the rise, the cottages stepping up it west to east — Mara & Pip's at the junction, the keeper's cottage with its herbs over the door and the brass lighter inside, Rowan's ledgers at the top — the lane ending at the hilltop bench with the whole village and valley falling away behind. A lamppost at every door, and the brook running down between the row and the square.
cameras._framing_note: RE-SOLVED AT 2x 2026-08-01, and the provisional frame is now a measured one. yaw 340 -> 290, pitch 42 -> 50. The old frame measured 65.6% of 64 probes against the current bundle; this one measures 84.4% and, uniquely among the five shots that were re-aimed this round, it CLEARS THE TOWN'S 50 px LEGIBILITY FLOOR (charPxFar 56 at a 28.4 m standoff, against 36 px at the old angle). Both moves are read off the same column: at yaw 340 visibility never passes 72% at any pitch, because the row's own trees stand between a south-east camera and the lane; swinging to 290 puts the camera BELOW THE RISE AND DUE SOUTH — which is the shot's own words, 'broadside to the home lane from below the rise' — and the pitch column there reads p30 58%, p34 73%, p42 81%, p46 83%, p50 84.4%, flattening at 50. The town-wide best is 87.5% at yaw 280/300 and costs 7 px, i.e. the legibility gate; 290/50 is the angle that holds both. THE HILLTOP-BENCH LEAD IS STILL OPEN and is now cheap to test: this camera stands 28 m out where the old one stood 44, so the bench view is a re-sweep, not a re-architecture. The note it replaces: PROVISIONAL, and the only frame in the set that was. yaw 225 put the camera 1.18 m inside veg_emb_hr_tree6_crown1 (0.0% of 64 probes). Home Row's geometry is still moving — hillside-cottage was searched to a new coordinate and the lane bowed above Rowan's house while this was being authored — so this frame is the best of the sweep re-run against the CLOSED master (64.1%, up from 35.9% at the frame baked before the trees moved) and is RE-SWEPT after the district freezes, together with the coordinator's hilltop-bench lead: from the bench the Heartlight and the brook's downhill run sit in the same east-south-east quadrant, and a wider lens may hold the flame and the town's name in one frame. If that fights exit-framing or the no-sliver floor, seam canon wins and the bench view goes on the board as a taste option.
cameras._owns_note: far-rooftops-nw and hillside-cottages are the implied-scale vista clusters west and north-west of the row (the map's own impliedScale ruling: non-walkable massing past every playable edge, composed INTO the frame). upper-lane-closed is the soft closure — the lane visibly continues NW past Lake's home and a festival cart stands in it.

cameras.name: The North Lane
cameras.shot: The walled climb. Side-on from over the pond, the lane running up the frame between its dry-stone walls from the square's north edge to the tithe barn, which is its landmark and its turn — cats in the rafters, harvest stores, and the back lane closed off with stacked Emberwake barrels. Above the barn the lane bends away east toward the gate court and the old edge of the village.
cameras._framing_note: RE-AIMED AGAIN, AND THIS TIME IT IS A GOOD SHOT. yaw 320 -> 350, pitch 54 -> 46: 58 px at 29.6 m, 79.7% of 64 probes, against 30 px one round ago. NOTHING ABOUT THE CAMERA CHANGED THE NUMBER — the shot gave up the 58 m quiet road it had been carrying (see `gateroad`) and its region fell from 16.2 x 55.3 m to 16.2 x 26 m, which is the whole 28-pixel move. yaw 350 is near enough to the intent's 'side-on from over the pond' to be it, and the pitch could come down 8 degrees because the shot is no longer trying to see round four bends of forest road: at 320/54 the same region still reads 55 px, so the bearing is chosen on composition — 350 stands the camera at the lane's foot and runs it up the frame between its walls, which is the shot's own sentence.
cameras._arrivals_why: NO OVERRIDE IS AUTHORED HERE AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Both of this shot's arrivals measure 0.0% visible against its own baked depth plate (tools/arrival_probe.py --town emberbrook): a player entering the north lane from the square or from the gate court MATERIALISES AS A GHOST. seam-canon 9.3 says measure why before choosing the fix, so it was measured three ways and all three agree the camera is not the row. (1) A ray-cast sweep of all 288 yaw/pitch candidates against both arrival points at chest and head height: no position in the town sees both, the best sees one. (2) The named occluders are emb_gt_barn_walls and emb_gt_barn_roof — this shot's own subject. (3) A search of every point on this shot's ground that clears all its bands by the full 1.6 m target returns 22 candidates per arrival and every one of them probes at 0.0% chest, because they all sit at the lane's north end behind the barn. THE CAUSE IS THE MAP: the tithe barn stands at (33,34), which is the lane's own terminus, and the gate-court arrival is 2 m past it. Moving the barn off the end of its lane fixes this shot and nothing else can. Logged rather than papered over with an override the probe would have refused.
cameras._owns_note: A TRANSIT SHOT THAT OWNS ITS OWN JUNCTION-SIDE LANDMARK. It is 18 m of climb with the barn on it; both of its ends (square-plaza, gate-court) belong to neighbours, which is the loop-stairs shape — but at 18 m each end gets ONE seam on flat ground with 12 m between them, where the loop stairs had to fit two inside seven. No `thresholdPair`: the second cut is never on the same edge as the first.

cameras.name: The Quiet Road
cameras.shot: The middle of the seclusion, and the shot where the village leaves you. The road curving north between the trees with the wood closed over it, no lamp, no fence, no cart, nothing anybody built — the barn's roofline gone behind the last bend and the gate not yet in front. The environment shift the seclusion round was measured into the map: this is the stretch it happens ON.
cameras._framing_note: ALONG THE ROAD FROM THE EAST SHOULDER, AND THE SECOND-CLEANEST SIGHTLINE IN THE TOWN: 57 px at 23.8 m, 100.0% of 64 probes. yaw 80 sets the camera off the outside of the road's curve so the bend is read as a bend — the road enters frame at one edge and leaves at the other, which is the only way 23 m of curving road tells a player where it goes. Pitch 10 keeps the wood closed over the top of frame, which is this shot's whole subject; the column at yaw 80 falls away above it (p10 57 px, p18 51, p26 47) because a higher camera looks over the trees the shot exists to be inside of.
cameras._owns_note: MINTED 2026-08-01 on the coordinator's shot-grammar ruling, and its span is set by SEAM CANON RATHER THAN BY THE SWEEP — which is the correction this shot exists to record. The costing that authorised it said 'the road as two shots reads 72 and 65 px'; that costing was wrong, because it never checked seam-canon 2. `barn__gate-court` is ONE map edge, 58.5 m of it, and walking one edge end to end may change the camera AT MOST ONCE — twice only for a declared `thresholdPair`, and never three times. Two shots ON the road means three cuts on that edge (barn -> road-a -> road-b -> court) and is illegal at any framing. THE LEGAL SHAPE IS THREE REGIONS AND TWO CUTS: `northlane` takes the road's first 30%, this shot the middle 40%, `gatefield` the last 30%, so the walk fires exactly two cuts, both on this edge, the second leaving the shot the first entered — the threshold pair's three conditions, satisfied by construction. It is the map's only thresholdPair and it earns the name literally: this shot IS a place you enter and leave. The split fractions were chosen by sweeping nine of them: 0.30/0.70 is the one that maximises the WORST of the three shots (64 / 70 / 54 px against 56 / 73 / 57 at 0.35/0.75, whose weakest shot clears the floor at 26 angles against 36).
cameras._environment_note: WHERE THE VILLAGE ACTUALLY GOES, MEASURED, because the seclusion stamp asserted it and nothing had checked it since the mill was re-ruled. Ray-cast from eye height at 41 points along the road to the apex of every one of the 58 village roof meshes south of y=70: the inn, the item shop and the infill roofs are gone by t=0.55 (32 m from the barn), the barn's own roof by t=0.725 (42 m) — and THE WATERMILL'S ROOF IS VISIBLE FROM THE GATE COURT ITSELF, at t=1.0, 64 m away. The stamp's claim of 'roofs strict-zero from 38.9 m' does not hold on the current build, and the cause is dated after it: the mill was re-ruled to a 4.4 m wheel with a ~12 m ridge at the 2x round. FILED FOR THE BUILDER/DRESSING LANE — the fix is forest, not camera. It does not move this shot's boundaries: the village-proper threshold at t=0.575 falls INSIDE this shot rather than on either of its cuts, which is the better cinema anyway. You do not cut at the moment of loss; you watch it happen.

cameras.name: The Old Gate
cameras.shot: Chapter One's set-piece stage, and the only unwarm frame in the town. The flag-stoned court from the south, facing the sealed gate square-on with its twin sigil plates in the ground before it, and the Whisperwood trailhead with its stile on the court's west rim. Behind on the left is NOT the barn any more but the wood the quiet road came out of. No lamp reaches here — nobody's warmth does — and after the seclusion stamp (306554a) nothing else does either: the barn is 63 m back down a curving forest road, the village is out of sight from 16.6 m past it, and the court reads gray against a horizon of trees rather than against a village that is all lamplight. RE-AIM AT THE DISTRICT PASS: the framing below was solved against a court at (76,74), and the yaw note's reasoning — Pond Lane's crowns closing the due-south sightline — is about geometry 50 m away that this shot can no longer see.
cameras._framing_note: yaw 270 -> 280, pitch 42 -> 46: 54 px at 28.2 m and 100.0% of 64 probes, still the only shot in the town at a perfect sightline. The eight degrees are the last 11.7 m of the quiet road, which this shot took off `gateroad` so that the road would carry two cuts and not three (seam-canon 2 allows a thresholdPair two and never three) — the region grew from 17.6 x 16.2 m to 17.9 x 20.9 m and the frame had to rise to hold it. THE COMPOSITION IS UNCHANGED AND CHECKED: the sealed gate at ndc (0.38, 0.83), the trailhead stile at (-0.05, 0.49), and BOTH SIGIL PLATES side by side just above centre at (0.29, 0.51) and (0.44, 0.48) — the chapter's co-op set piece, framed, with the doors behind it. The 20-degree deviation this shot carried through the 1x era stays withdrawn: the Pond Lane crowns that forced it are 60 m behind the camera since the seclusion stamp.
cameras._owns_note: SECLUSION STAMP 306554a: the back path `washline-green__gate-court` IS WITHDRAWN FROM THE MAP, and this shot's reference to it goes with it — a camera cannot own an edge that no longer exists, and cine_regions proves coverage by matching these strings against the map's own records. What the ownership bought (the town's second loop carrying exactly one seam, at the green's end on the flat rather than on the climb) went with the edge: with the Old Gate 63 m out in the wood there is no village loop to it at all, and the loop is now square -> pond -> green -> barn -> square. The single way to the gate is `barn__gate-court`, 58 m of quiet wooded road owned by `northlane` — ONE camera on a 58 m road is a district-pass question, not a coverage failure, and it is filed as one. downstream-vista is the river bending into the hills past the gate — where Vesper's maps point, and not walkable.
